issue.title: Every bob capture (and each Mac live preview) eagerly reads the whole vault via DependencyContext::new
issue.description:
## What is wrong

Every `bob capture` batch, including each Bob Mac Capture live-preview `bob capture --dry-run`, reads and parses the whole vault before planning anything, even for a plain `hello` draft that never touches a dependency.

- Root cause: `src/native/capture/plan.rs:84` builds `DependencyContext::new(&request.bob_dir, today)` unconditionally for every batch. `DependencyContext::new` (`src/native/capture/dependencies.rs:43-61`) calls `capture_dependency_tasks::discover(bob_dir)` eagerly. That function reads every Markdown note (`fs::read_to_string`), task-scans it, and computes block-ID suggestions for every task that lacks an ID.
- Introduced by 6718111 (2026-10-03, "implement staged capture writer with dependency parsing").
- `!note:block-id` items then read the whole vault a second time: `staged_snapshot_for_recovery` → `DependencyContext::recovery_base_snapshot` (`dependencies.rs:65-86`) walks and re-reads every note.

## Evidence (apollo, warm page cache, copy of the live vault: 6,207 .md files, 13.4 MB)

Measured with a release build of master b566ba4:

| draft (`bob capture --dry-run --format json`) | eager (HEAD) | discover skipped (prototype hack) | tiny vault (5 notes) |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `hello` | 0.22-0.27 s | 0.04 s | <0.01 s |
| `=x` | 0.28 s | 0.04 s | 0.01 s |
| `!sase:fix-apollo` | 0.37-0.41 s | (needs resolver) | 0.02 s |

- `strace -e openat`: `hello` opens 5,071 vault .md files; `!sase:fix-apollo` opens 10,125, because the vault is read twice.
- `strace -k` puts the reads in `bob_cli::native::capture_dependency_tasks::discover`.
- Raw costs for comparison: a sequential `cat` of all notes takes 0.19 s; a directory walk plus stat takes 0.03 s; a parallel `rg -l dependsOn` takes 0.03 s.

## Impact

Bob Mac Capture spawns `capture --dry-run` after every 50 ms typing pause (`CapturePanelModel.swift` debounce). Almost all of each preview's latency is now spent reading notes the draft never uses. This contradicts the thin-client decision's "~5 ms dry-run spawn" premise. Every CLI capture and submit pays the same cost.

## Suggested fix

- Build `DependencyContext.discovered` lazily, only when an item needs it (`&`, `!`, a selected/explicit dependent).
- Resolve `!`/`&` notes from a walk-only `NoteIndex` where possible.
- Share one batch-scoped vault snapshot between discovery and `!` dependent recovery so the vault is read at most once.
- Optionally read in parallel, with a `memchr` prefilter (`dependsOn`, `id::`) so only candidate notes are parsed for recovery.

Add a regression test that a plain capture does not read unrelated notes (for example, a fixture with an unreadable or poisoned note that only discovery would touch).

task_type_fields.impact: Every capture and every Bob Mac Capture live-preview spawn pays ~0.2 s (apollo) of vault I/O it does not use; '!' items read the vault twice (~0.4 s).
task_type_fields.repro: BOB_DIR=<full vault copy> BOB_NOW='2026-10-09 10:10:00' bob capture --dry-run --format json -- 'hello' takes ~0.25 s and strace shows 5,071 .md opens; the same command against a 5-note vault takes <0.01 s, and a build with discovery skipped takes 0.04 s on the full vault.

issue.creation_reason: Found while researching auto-linking unblocked dependents: capture latency on the full vault is ~95% unused dependency discovery, and the new feature must not add a second vault read on top of it.
